This is an ordinary suit for recovery of damages of Rs.74,26,000/- with pendent-lite and future interest @ 18% per annum and cost.

2. The plaintiff, trades in dry fruits by purchasing dry dates, ginger and other commodities during crop season by keeping the same in cold storage and thereafter the commodities are sold whenever the price is high.
The defendant is a private limited company having a cold storage located at Narela Road, Sonepat, Haryana which it leases out to various parties for storing their goods.

The plaintiff also used to avail the cold storage facility of the defendant by storing all kinds of commodities including perishable agricultural goods and whenever the stocks were demanded back by the plaintiff, the defendant used to release the same on time.

From 22.6.2021 to 11.04.2023, he stored following perishable goods in the cold storage of the defendant:-

sentences.text: In earlier suit, the plaintiff moved an application U/o 12 Rule 6 CPC on 19.02.2024 for decree due to admission of defendant that some goods were lying at its cold storage.
Vide order dated 15.03.2024, the court allowed plaintiff to collect those goods after paying or bearing the transportation charges.

Consequently, the plaintiff paid cold storage and transportation charges and collected goods on 21.03.2024 and then the suit was withdrawn on 12.04.2024.
The dry ginger has life more than four years and during that whole period, it maintains aroma and flavour depending upon storage conditions.
The defendant being owner of a cold storage division was entrusted goods to preserve the same in good condition.
Perhaps he did not take care of the goods properly.
Subsequently there was spike in the price of ginger due to which the intention of the defendant became dishonest and he sold the goods in open market.

He had purchased the stored ginger from Sagar which is of best quality and the price of that ginger from 26.02.2024 to 03.03.2024 was Rs.390/- - Rs.425/- per kg and during 25.03.2024 to 31.03.2024 the price was Rs.390/- - Rs.400/- per kg.

The defendant mis-appropriated 359 bags + 200 bags = Rs.559 bags of ginger, each bag was containing 35 kg and in this way the total quantity of ginger was Digitally signed by CS (COMM) No.6563/24 UMED Sanjay Kumar Proprietor of M/s Sanjay UMED SINGH Date:
Enterprises Vs M/s Ambe Agro & Cold Storage SINGH Page No.4to25 2025.06.09 16:26:32 +0530 559 bags x 35 kg = 19,565 kg

As the price of ginger was Rs.400/- per kg by selling the ginger in open market, the defendant caused loss of kg 19,565/- x Rs.400/- = 78,26,000/- to the plaintiff and for recovery of that amount, the defendant was given notice on 18.04.2024 which went unheard.
3. The defendant came out with the case that the goods mentioned in para no.8 of plaint were received in their cold storage for preservation on various dates.

The goods i.e dry giner were perishable in nature and with the passage of time, their quality started deteriorating and the plaintiff was intimated on time to take the delivery but he was in greed and insisted defendant to keep on preserving the same for longer period as by doing so the plaintiff might have got huge benefit if the rate of ginger spiked.

It is reiterated that the defendant's officials and directors time and again informed plaintiff that the ginger preserved in storage on 22.06.2021 (359 bages) and on 17.04.2022 (200 bags) were in bad condition and he was requested to take the delivery but he did not pay any heed.
Due to not taking back the delivery in time, the ginger got spoiled completely due to which the garbage was removed from the cold storage and hence defendant is not bound to pay even a single penny.

sentences.text: The plaintiff took delivery of admitted stock and thereafter the defendant was asked to return 359 bags but the same was not returned.
In fact, during 2023 and 2024, there was a huge appreciation in the price due to which the defendant turned dishonest and sold it in open market.

Though his client had purchased ginger only at price of Rs.100/- and Rs.60/- per kg from Sagar, Madhya Pradesh, but in 2023 and 2024, the rate increased to Rs.390/-
to Rs.450/- per kg.
Due to non return of bailed goods, the defendant is liable to bear the loss caused to plaintiff.
The loss per kg is Rs.400/- and total quantity usurped by defendant is 18865 kg and

hence the plaintiff is entitled to kg.18865 x Rs.400/- =
Rs.75,46,000/- with interest and cost.
In this regard, he heavily relied upon some newspaper reports in which the price of dry ginger has been quoted from Rs.390/- to Rs.450/- per kg during 2023 and 2024.
9. On the other hand, counsel for defendant argued that plaintiff is a black marketeer as he used to purchase commodities at less price and sell at a huge price.
He admitted that the plaintiff had preserved 359 bags and 200 bags of dry ginger with defendant on 22.06.2021 and 17.04.2022 but it was destroyed and hence it was disposed of.

Before doing so, the plaintiff was intimated several times that the commodity was in the process of deterioration and that he should left it but he became greedy as Digitally signed by CS (COMM) No.6563/24 Sanjay Kumar Proprietor of M/s Sanjay UMED UMED SINGH Date:

sentences.text: The tax invoice Ex.PW1/6 dated 21.06.2021 shows that the plaintiff had purchased 200 bags of dry ginger (Sonth) from M/s Gauri Shankar Satish Kumar, Gali Arya Samaj, Naya Bans, Delhi-110006 at a price of Rs.100/- per kg.
and each bag contained 35 kg.
In the same way, he purchased 159 bags from the same person on 22.06.2021 vide invoice Ex.PW1/5 in Rs.100/- per kg and again each bag contained 35 kg.
The total of both invoices comes out to Rs.13,19,325/-.
The statement of HDFC Bank Ex.PW1/7 of the plaintiff shows that he had paid that amount to the seller namely M/s Gauri Shankar Satish Kumar, Gali Arya Samaj, Naya Bans, Delhi-110006 on 21.06.2022.
He purchased 440 bags, each containing 30 kg @ Rs.70/- per kg from Hari Om Traders, Khari Baoli on 17.04.2022 vide invoice Ex.PW1/8.
The statement Ex.PW1/9 of HDFC Bank of the plaintiff shows that invoice amount of Rs.97,200/- was paid to seller Hariom Trader on 22.04.2022.
It becomes clear from above discussion that the purchase price of 359 bags was Rs.100/- per kg and of 200 bags, was Rs.70/- per kg.
